newsitem.title: INDIA: India's RBI chief sees rupee staying stable.
newsitem.headline: India's RBI chief sees rupee staying stable.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India governor Chakravarty Rangarajan said on Monday he expected the rupee to remain stable around current levels.
"As of now the demand/supply situation is well balanced and the rupee will remain basically stable around this level," the central bank chief said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Asked what rate of depreciation the RBI was looking for Rangarajan replied, "I'm not looking for any rate of depreciation."

"All that I would say is that we do look into the real effective exchange rate because that has some impact on the competitiveness of India exports," the central bank chief added. The rupee currently stands at 35.65 per dollar.

Rangarajan also said he expected inflation to stay between six to seven percent. Inflation, measured by the wholesale price index was running at 6.3 percent year-on-year on September 28, compared with a year-ago level of 8.8 percent.
Ranagarajan also said he expected M3 monetary growth to stay within the target zone of 15.5 to 16.0 percent. M3 growth on September 27 showed a year-on-year growth of 15.3 percent.
The RBI outlined its credit policy for the second half of 1996/97 on Saturday, and announced measures to add liquidity to the banking system to bring down interest rates.
